pr_body:
These changes makes it so that tidb can also compile for ARM, with for instance:

    GOOS=linux GOARCH=arm GOARM=7 go build

### What problem does this PR solve?

Issue Number: close #54247 

Problem Summary:

### What changed and how does it work?

Changing `int` to `int64` a couple of places in `parser/mysql/const.go` and `parser/mysql/util.go`.

The length of int is shorter on ARM7 than on x86_64.

### Check List

Tests <!-- At least one of them must be included. -->

- [ ] Unit test
- [ ] Integration test
- [x] Manual test (add detailed scripts or steps below)
- [ ] No need to test
  > - [ ] I checked and no code files have been changed.
  > <!-- Or your custom  "No need to test" reasons -->

I am using `tidb` in [Algernon](https://github.com/xyproto/algernon), and the proposed changes made it compile.

How I tested it:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/xyproto/algernon
cd algernon
go get -v github.com/pingcap/tidb@master
go mod tidy
go mod vendor
cd vendor/github.com/pingcap/tidb
curl -o arm.patch 'https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/commit/cc5f0b180c4f9609af02c3f628412f0a75bd73fa.diff'
patch -p1 -i arm.patch
cd ../../../..
GOOS=linux GOARCH=arm GOARM=7 go build -mod=vendor
```

Running `make` also works:

```
~/clones/tidb master ≡
❯ make
CGO_ENABLED=1  GO111MODULE=on go build -tags codes  -ldflags '-X "github.com/pingcap/tidb/pkg/parser/mysql.TiDBReleaseVersion=cc5f0b180c" -X "github.com/pingcap/tidb/pkg/util/versioninfo.TiDBBuildTS=2024-08-06 14:17:59" -X "github.com/pingcap/tidb/pkg/util/versioninfo.TiDBGitHash=cc5f0b180c4f9609af02c3f628412f0a75bd73fa" -X "github.com/pingcap/tidb/pkg/util/versioninfo.TiDBGitBranch=master" -X "github.com/pingcap/tidb/pkg/util/versioninfo.TiDBEdition=Community" ' -o bin/tidb-server ./cmd/tidb-server
Build TiDB Server successfully!
```

I tried replacing values in Makefiles in order to build and test with `GOOS=linux GOARCH=arm GOARM=7` but could not find the best approach.

I'm not quite sure how to *properly* test the proposed changes.

Side effects

- [ ] Performance regression: Consumes more CPU
- [ ] Performance regression: Consumes more Memory
- [ ] Breaking backward compatibility

Documentation

- [ ] Affects user behaviors
- [ ] Contains syntax changes
- [x] Contains variable changes
- [ ] Contains experimental features
- [x] Changes MySQL compatibility

I assume that these changes do not change MySQL compatibility, but since it touches files related to MySQL I checked the box, nevertheless.

```release-note
None
```

issue_context.title: cannot use 1 << iota (untyped int constant 2147483648) as SQLMode value in constant declaration (overflows)
issue_context.body:
Hi,

tidb does not compile for ARM 6 or 7, for instance when building with `GOARM=7 GOOS=linux GOARCH=arm go build`:

```
# github.com/pingcap/tidb/pkg/parser/mysql
vendor/github.com/pingcap/tidb/pkg/parser/mysql/const.go:462:2: cannot use 1 << iota (untyped int constant 2147483648) as SQLMode value in constant declaration (overflows)
vendor/github.com/pingcap/tidb/pkg/parser/mysql/const.go:463:2: cannot use 1 << iota (untyped int constant 4294967296) as SQLMode value in constant declaration (overflows)
vendor/github.com/pingcap/tidb/pkg/parser/mysql/util.go:44:19: cannot use 4294967295 (untyped int constant) as int value in struct literal (overflows)
vendor/github.com/pingcap/tidb/pkg/parser/mysql/util.go:45:19: cannot use 4294967295 (untyped int constant) as int value in struct literal (overflows)
```

After making these changes, tidb compiles again, but I am not sure that it keeps the correct behavior:

```
diff --git a/vendor/github.com/pingcap/tidb/pkg/parser/mysql/const.go b/vendor/github.com/pingcap/tidb/pkg/parser/mysql/const.go
index c9862fb5..768355f8 100644
--- a/vendor/github.com/pingcap/tidb/pkg/parser/mysql/const.go
+++ b/vendor/github.com/pingcap/tidb/pkg/parser/mysql/const.go
@@ -16,6 +16,7 @@ package mysql
 import (
        "fmt"
        "strings"
+       "math"

        "github.com/pingcap/errors"
        "github.com/pingcap/tidb/pkg/parser/format"
@@ -428,7 +429,7 @@ func SetSQLMode(ori SQLMode, add SQLMode) SQLMode {
 // consts for sql modes.
 // see https://dev.mysql.com/doc/internals/en/query-event.html#q-sql-mode-code
 const (
-       ModeRealAsFloat SQLMode = 1 << iota
+       ModeRealAsFloat SQLMode = math.MaxUint16
        ModePipesAsConcat
        ModeANSIQuotes
        ModeIgnoreSpace
diff --git a/vendor/github.com/pingcap/tidb/pkg/parser/mysql/util.go b/vendor/github.com/pingcap/tidb/pkg/parser/mysql/util.go
index c69e2903..a2c0ac70 100644
--- a/vendor/github.com/pingcap/tidb/pkg/parser/mysql/util.go
+++ b/vendor/github.com/pingcap/tidb/pkg/parser/mysql/util.go
@@ -13,6 +13,8 @@

 package mysql

+import "math"
+
 type lengthAndDecimal struct {
        length  int
        decimal int
@@ -41,8 +43,8 @@ var defaultLengthAndDecimal = map[byte]lengthAndDecimal{
        TypeTinyBlob:   {255, 0},
        TypeBlob:       {65535, 0},
        TypeMediumBlob: {16777215, 0},
-       TypeLongBlob:   {4294967295, 0},
-       TypeJSON:       {4294967295, 0},
+       TypeLongBlob:   {math.MaxUint16, 0},
+       TypeJSON:       {math.MaxUint16, 0},
        TypeNull:       {0, 0},
        TypeSet:        {-1, 0},
        TypeEnum:       {-1, 0},
```


8.0.11-TiDB-None
comments:
> cannot use 1 << iota (untyped int constant 2147483648) as SQLMode value in constant declaration (overflows)

Maybe it's better to change the underlying type `SQLMode` from `int` to `int64`.

```diff
-       ModeRealAsFloat SQLMode = 1 << iota
+       ModeRealAsFloat SQLMode = math.MaxUint16
```

`iota` has special meaning, it should not be changed 

https://go.dev/ref/spec#Iota
Sure, I have no opinion on what the best fix is.

review_comments: This will truncate the value. Does your application need to change the return value `flen` to int64?

My application does not need `flen` to be `int` or `int64` in particular, only that the code compiles and runs also on ARM7, ideally.

I had a couple of experiments with this, where I tried changing the return value to `int64`. But, this has a couple of issues:

* A change from `int` to `int64` has a "domino-effect", where the type changes needs to be propagated throughout many files. It also breaks tests.
* Ideally, the length of something should not be a signed integer, but perhaps `uint64`.
* For the code to be idiomatic Go, `-1` should not be used to indicate an error or a missing value, but an error should be returned instead. `-1` is currently used in several places, making an introduction of `uint64` a larger change.

So yes, ideally, `uint`, `uint32` or `uint64` should be used instead of `int` or `int64` for lengths all over the code base, but that is a small project all of its own.
